newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell's Wavin says mulls listing.
newsitem.headline: Shell's Wavin says mulls listing.

text.p: Plastics maker Wavin BV, a 50 percent owned unit of Royal Dutch/Shell, said on Monday it might apply for listing in the long term.
"I can imagine the shareholders will decide to modify the structure somewhere in the next century," chairman Fons Driessen told reporters.
But he stressed he did not expect a listing in the short term.
Wavin, Europe's largest plastic pipes maker, operates through 34 outlets in 19 European countries and has some 5,000 employees. It plans to grow inside and outside Europe.
Earlier, the company said it expected Wafin's 1996 net profit to have increased by about 60 percent from the 21.1 million guilders earned in 1995.
Wafin was created in 1955 on the initiative of the regional utility Waterpipes Company Overijssel (WMO), which needed non-leaking water pipes.
At the time of the creation, WMO and metal pipes production plant Excelsior in the Dutch town of Schiedam shared Wafin on equal terms.
In 1962, Royal Dutch/Shell bought Excelsior's 50 percent stake in Wafin, leaving the WMO with the balance.
